headline: Governance Grows Up
thesis: From CoSN's screen-time principles to agentic-AI controls in production, edtech's governance layer is hardening — while Washington presses colleges on data and international students head to court.
summary: Wednesday's news clusters around maturing oversight. CoSN published three principles for school screen-time policies, student delegates in Boston issued their own K-12 AI-policy recommendations, and a new survey finds agentic AI moving from pilot to production with governance controls front and center. Security researchers warn AI has entered the live attack chain, accelerating familiar K-12 cyber threats. In higher ed, the Education Department says 42 percent of colleges haven't fully submitted required student-outcomes data, a lawsuit challenges the new length-of-stay limit for international students, and Handshake data shows AI career skills spreading well beyond computer science. 1EdTech hosts its assessment-to-achievement webinar today, with accessibility and digital-credentials sessions close behind.
footnote: Compiled from 11 curated edtech sources · August 19, 2026 · Education Technology Insights blocks automated access; its items and some evergreen entries are listed without fresh dates.
